title: Orchestra prober suite: deterministic capacity‑proving harness and SLA attestation playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a production‑grade load and benchmarking harness ("Orchestra Prober") plus an operator playbook used for Dedicated capacity certification and customer acceptance. The goal is to provide deterministic, tenant‑aware capacity proofs that combine replayed production traffic, synthetic microburst profiles, and KV/prefix cache warmup stages to produce reproducible throughput and tail‑latency signatures. Deliverables: (1) load prober service and test harness code in GitHub, (2) methodology doc for how we compute throughput guarantees (qps, tokens/s, and 95/99/99.9 latency curves), (3) an acceptance checklist and runbook operators and Solutions Engineering can use during customer pilots and handoffs.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run a 3‑stage scenario: cold start, warmup (cache prefill), steady state sustain for 30m with configurable tenant mixes
Measured metrics include 50/95/99/99.9 latency percentiles, p50 token/sec, sustained tokens/sec, succeeded requests %, and QoS violations per minute
Autoscaling policy validation: can exercise scale‑up and scale‑down triggers deterministically and verify no >2x SLA breaches on scale events
Reproducibility: given the same seed and profile, runs on identical infra should have <5% variance in sustained throughput and <10% variance in 99th latency
Customer acceptance checklist documented with sample evidence bundle (metrics, flamegraphs, PRs and run artifacts)
implementation_steps: Design workload profiles (tenant mixes, prompt length distributions, KV cache hit ratio targets) — see confluence draft
Implement modular prober service (drivers: replay, synthetic microburst, constant qps) and orchestrator (scenario composer, seedable RNG)
Add telemetry hooks for token accounting, request tracing, kernel selection flags, and autoscaler event tagging
Create validation pipeline that runs a baseline on 'canary' pool + run on target dedicated fleet; collect deterministic artifacts (traces, histograms, heap/CPU profiles)
Integrate run artifact bundler and short presigned upload flow for customer evidence attachments
Write operator playbook with step‑by‑step customer acceptance flow and automated gating script that fails noisy runs
decisions: Use mixed approach: production replay for realistic behavior + synthetic microbursts for worst‑case tail exposure
Replay driver will be tenant‑aware and support anonymized request payloads; we will not use raw customer PII during standard cert runs
Latency percentiles used for SLA attestation: p95, p99, p99.9. SLOs will be expressed as 95% of windows meeting latency thresholds over a 24h run for certification
Autoscaler validation will rely on event tagging instead of direct scaling time assertions to avoid noise across clouds
risks: Infra noise: cloud interference could inflate variance; mitigations: dedicate a quiet test pool and run multiple seeds
Data privacy: replays must avoid customer PII — enforce anonymization and approval process
Resource cost: extended runs to prove stability are expensive — tighten default run durations and make longer runs opt‑in for customers
False confidence: synthetic profiles alone can miss real tenant mixes — require at least one replayed customer sample for certification
run_plan: Phase 1: unit harness + CI smoke (run on dev cluster, <10m) — PR #214
Phase 2: deterministic baseline on canary fleet (3 runs, different seeds) — collect variance metrics
Phase 3: certified run on dedicated pool with Solutions Eng present — gather evidence bundle
Phase 4: customer pilot run guided by playbook; produce acceptance artifact for customer signoff
blockers: Quota: need a dedicated canary pool allocation from Infra (ticket INF-2025-58)
Telemetry: backend must expose token accounting API (ENG-993322) before final evidence bundling
Legal: anonymization checklist signoff required for replay driver (security/legal review pending)
